_about: getEndUser answers that the app's gate (backend/services/identity_lookup._cii_parse) and the Mac's persona self-check (deploy/lab5/lab5_cii.parse_end_user) must read the same way. expect: found (details, no error), not_found (CII's 'no such user': no error at all, and getEndUser null or a present, null endUserDetails), unavailable (anything else, every answer that carries an error included, whatever the error says and whatever code it carries). No error at all is errors absent, null or an empty list; any other errors value carries one, an empty object, an empty string, 0 or false included. An unavailable case may carry trust, failing and reasons: what a partial answer did say, which the gate keeps and still blocks on (reasons: its block; none: nothing against the user), while the self-check reads every unavailable answer as a failed query. error_messages and coded_errors are errors tried in every shape of error_shapes (coded_errors puts each of its codes in each of its places), each unavailable with nothing learned. If spikes S5/S6 show CII answers a login it has no record of with an error, that exact answer is added here as not_found and matched exactly in both copies, never by its words or by a code. No table lists every message or code a rule could key on, so tests/test_identity_personas.py also pins each copy's first statement, which turns away every answer that carries an error before anything reads it, and the path to it: each side's fetch hands its parser CII's answer untouched, and each parser answers nothing but a failure between the rule and its errors guard. Run by tests/test_identity_gate.py and tests/test_identity_personas.py.

error_shapes._about: Where an error in a getEndUser answer sits, each tried with every message of error_messages and every error coded_errors builds: on getEndUser (getEndUser null), on its endUserDetails (getEndUser an object, endUserDetails null), on getEndUser with data null (the shape the published schema gives such an error: getEndUser returns the non-null GetEndUserOutput!, so an error on it nulls the whole of data), and with no path (data null).

shapes.where: on getEndUser, data null (its non-null GetEndUserOutput! failed)

error_messages._about: Messages of a code-less error, each tried in every shape of error_shapes. Every one is unavailable, whatever it says: the first ones read like CII saying 'no such user', the rest are about something else (a permission, a scope, a role, a pool, a session, another principal). No error is ever read as that answer by its words.

coded_errors._about: Errors that carry a code, built by tests/cii_end_user_answers.coded_errors: each code of codes in each place of places, alone and then in all of them at once, on each message of messages, then the errors listed here (two different codes on one error). So a code is tried in every place, never only where an entry happened to put it. The whole-path checks (the gate's lookup and decision, the Mac's CIIClient.end_user) put them on every message the table holds instead (cii_end_user_answers.all_messages: this section's, error_messages and those of cases), so no code and no message the table holds go untried together; the box's victim row and the self-check's row keep this section's messages. Each is tried, with its path from the shape, in every shape of error_shapes, data null on getEndUser (the published schema's shape) included. The places are where GraphQL servers commonly put a code: extensions.code (Apollo Server, Hasura), extensions.errorType (Netflix DGS), extensions.classification (graphql-java, Spring for GraphQL), and errorType (AppSync) and type (GitHub's GraphQL API) on the error itself. The codes are not found, user not found and end user not found, each spelled four ways (NOT_FOUND, NotFound, not-found, not_found), and two refusals. Every one is unavailable, whatever its code says and wherever the code sits: a code that reads 'not found' or 'user not found' is still an error, and no error is ever 'no such user' (a refused API client can carry one, as on the permission message here). An answer spikes S5/S6 pin as CII's own goes to cases, matched exactly.
